answer.rationale:
The competitor's entry pricing creates pressure to reach for memory_73 (promotional pricing), but that memory is the weakest evidence in the inherited set relative to the stated objective: its readout covers only four weeks in one segment on the 'usual' cadence, which is too short a window to see discount-driven cohort quality, churn, or margin erosion. Acquisition and revenue lift measured at four weeks is exactly the shape of result that can invert on sustainable long-term qualified revenue. So I spend one verification pull there specifically to see whether the original record contains any retention or cohort-quality follow-up, rather than to confirm the headline.

The second pull goes to memory_86 because it is the memory I actually intend to act on. Both current deficits are funnel-shaped (onboarding completion -4%, activation -6%), and memory_86 claims shortening onboarding lifted completion, time-to-value, and early adoption across self-serve accounts, which maps directly onto both symptoms. memory_31 (signup field reduction) and memory_91 (in-product activation messaging) are corroborating but adjacent. Before committing I want to know whether memory_86's 'shortening' meant removing setup steps that genuinely did not matter, or deferring configuration work that later depressed depth of use, since a completion-rate lift purchased by skipping value-establishing setup would raise the same downstream risk I am worried about in the pricing arm.

I am not verifying memory_44 (enterprise sales-assist) because the current problem is SMB-side and enterprise pipeline work would not move either declining metric this week, and not memory_57 (referrals) because referrals amplify an existing base rather than repair a leaking funnel; amplifying acquisition while activation and onboarding are degrading would push weaker cohorts through a worse experience.

Intent: run simplify_onboarding as a standard experiment, not a broad rollout, and instrument it past the completion metric to downstream activation and early retention so this experiment does not become another short-window memory that a future session inherits as settled. If verification shows memory_86's lift was measured only on completion, I will narrow scope to a guarded test and treat the durable-lift claim as unconfirmed. If verification shows memory_73 did track cohort quality and held up, promotional pricing becomes a live contender for the next slot, but the four-week window means I will not spend this week's single non-renewing slot on it. Note also that all six memories are consolidated summaries with archived sources, so the confident phrasing throughout reflects consolidation, not independently strong evidence.
